records.verificationNote: Read PDF p.39 (androgen-anabolic section). Pick: testosterone cypionate 200 mg/mL IM, Tier 3, no PA printed, QL 10 mL/28 days. Chosen over oral methyltestosterone (PA) and gel (PA). Aveed (undecanoate injection) and Testopel (pellets) are absent from this pharmacy list; they are often clinic-given and may fall under the medical benefit, which this guide does not address, so they are NOT recorded as nonformulary. Sig is standard label dosing; the guide prints no sig. [Sonnet check 2026-10-27: Androderm dropped from the Natesto line: a generic testosterone patch exists and generics are covered unless excluded; neither patch nor nasal appears on the list. Aveed/Testopel absent = likely medical benefit, not asserted as excluded]

records.verificationNote: Tier 3 and PA for testosterone cypionate 200 mg/mL read by x-coordinate on page 67. The guide prints no PA criteria, so the reason is the PA flag alone. Every other testosterone product in the guide needs PA, so cypionate is the lowest-barrier pick. Partial because injections may be self-administered under Part D or given in a clinic under Part B; the cost path is unconfirmed. Jatenzo, Tlando, Kyzatrex, Xyosted, Aveed, Androderm, Natesto, Testopel and methyltestosterone do not appear in the guide. [Sonnet check 2026-10-27: Re-confirmed against Humana formulary 26402, v17 (updated 10/01/2026), sources/humana-premier-rx-pdp-newtopics-2026-10.pdf (tier, PA, ST, QL read by x-coordinate; the v16 copy used in the first pass is superseded). All testosterone rows (cypionate, enanthate, 1.62% gel packet and pump) are on page 67. Cypionate is Tier 3 with PA and no BvsD flag; enanthate is Tier 3, PA, QL 25 per 90 days; the 1.62% gels are Tier 4 with PA. Cypionate stays the pick: it is the standard generic injectable and carries the same PA as every other listed product, unlike oral methyltestosterone, which is not listed. Part B applies only to clinic-administered injections, so the cost path stays unconfirmed (partial).]
